properties.statement: `--shared` TURNED SESSION-LOCAL METRICS INTO SHARED-STATE METRICS WITHOUT CHANGING THEIR INTERFACE, AND TWO BOSSES ATTRIBUTED A FLEET-WIDE MOVEMENT TO THEIR OWN CHANGE — IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION. loop_status and graph_report read IDENTICALLY before and after the migration; only the MEANING of their numbers changed. A total is now a fleet number moved by every attached boss and worker, wearing the timestamp of whoever asked. MEASURED on one graph in one day by non-coordinating sessions: defects 42 -> 6 -> 5 -> 12 (the 5 -> 12 arriving an hour later to a session that had done nothing at all), and gaps 48 -> 55 -> 69. api-boss `5d608b85` reported '42 -> 6' to the user TWICE as their own result; it was not. A worker checking in reported gaps 55 -> 69 and defects 12 -> 26 between two check-ins hours apart and, correctly, could name no cause. CONSEQUENCE THE REPORTER DREW AND IT IS THE GENERAL ONE: every citation of these counts written before `--shared` is now subtly wrong, and nothing in the output says so. THE ROOT SHAPE, in their words: A SESSION CANNOT TELL THAT IT IS NOT ALONE. Nothing in any payload reports concurrency — no attached-session count, no last-write-by — so every seat reasons as if solo and the output actively encourages it. They fixed it with a fleet convention (state whether a count is FLEET or SCOPED), which is a discipline layered on top of a tool that could just say it; a caveat maintained in a downstream doc is a defect routed around rather than fixed. ---- 2026-08-08, w-9d1d1499 (LANE PROSE-JOIN) ADDS THE CLEANEST INSTANCE YET AND THE COST OF THE WORKAROUND. loop_status read `67 gaps / 26 defects / 19 unproven` at their check-in and `48 / 27 / 14` hours later. THEY EXECUTED ZERO DESIGN WRITES THE ENTIRE SESSION, so none of that movement was theirs — AND THE ONLY WAY TO SAY SO IS A PARAGRAPH OF ENGLISH ASSERTING IT, WHICH THE NEXT READER HAS TO TAKE ON TRUST. Their PROTOCOL now carries a standing rule (§🔒 rule 5) whose ENTIRE CONTENT IS *'a global graph count is a fleet number, never your result'* — A DOCTRINE RULE EXISTING SOLELY TO COMPENSATE FOR SOMETHING THE TOOL COULD REPORT DIRECTLY. That is the second binding fleet rule written to work around one reflow2 output in as many days (see fact:defect-loop-status-next-routes-to-the-destructive-skill and its stop-order), and the pattern is the finding: when a tool will not say something, a downstream constitution grows a rule that everyone must remember instead. THEIR FIX SHAPE IS SHARPER THAN THE ORIGINAL: let loop_status/graph_report optionally take a `contributor_id` (or use the seat) and return *'changed since your first call this session: N, of which yours: M'*. THE DATA IS ALREADY THERE — authored_by, seats, ChangeEvents. It would replace a rule everyone must remember with a number anyone can cite. RELATED AND SEPARATELY REPORTED: there is no 'what changed since I looked, and by whom' query — sessions discover the graph moved by re-running a rollup and noticing a different number, which is the worst possible detector, and for ephemeral seats that die on context exhaustion the first real question on return is exactly 'what happened while I was gone'. That requirement is now ACCEPTED here as req:what-changed-since-i-looked-and-by-whom, and NOTHING SATISFIES IT (gap:e1a591cdc38809a5). FIX SHAPE: have loop_status/graph_report label their own rollups as graph-wide and report the number of currently-attached sessions; a scoped detect_gaps/detect_defects is already attributable and could say so.
